walkthroughs.body_html:
Sociology Basics: Key Concepts & Processes — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sociology Basics: Key Concepts & Processes brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sociology Basics: Key Concepts & Processes.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who argued the family had become symmetrical in 1973?
options: Murdock
Parsons
Young and Willmott
Oakley

mcqs.q: Murdock (1949) identified how many family functions?
What does Parsons mean by 'meritocracy' in education?
options: Everyone gets equal outcomes regardless of effort.
A reconstituted family is a family living in temporary housing.
Rewards and roles are allocated based on individual achievement.
Only middle-class students can succeed.
A reconstituted family is a family living in temporary housing.
A family formed when partners with children from previous relationships come together — a 'blended' or step-family — one of several family forms recognised in family diversity literature.

A reconstituted family is one that has been put back together after divorce.

mcqs.q: How did Marx define social class?
options: By relationship to the means of production: the bourgeoisie own productive resources; the proletariat sell their labour. Class is a structural relationship, not just income level.
Marx defined class by how much money people earn.
Marx defined class by occupational status like the Registrar General.
